text: Ugh, here come the tears again. Seriously, why do onions do this?
When you cut an onion, it breaks open cells - and an enzyme inside meets sulfur compounds, making a gas that's rough on your eyes.
That gas floats up, reaches your eyes, and mixes with your tears - turning into something that actually stings.
That's why chilling an onion, or using a sharper knife, cuts down on the tears. Cold slows the enzyme down, and a sharp blade bursts fewer cells.
Garlic has the same sulfur compounds, but it barely makes you cry. It just doesn't release a gas that travels up to your eyes.
So your eyes start to sting, and your body automatically floods them with tears to wash it out.
